doc_description: This document is a comprehensive installation and operation manual for the ACF5000 multi-component FTIR emission monitoring system, detailing safety instructions, system components, installation procedures, commissioning, maintenance, and shutdown protocols, with a strong emphasis on compliance with safety standards and proper handling of hazardous gases and equipment.

structure.title: Preface
structure.summary: The partial document is an installation manual for the ACF5000 multi-component FTIR emission monitoring system. It outlines the contents and structure of the manual, including safety instructions, intended use, system description, components, preparation for installation, installation procedures, commissioning, inspection, maintenance, and shutdown procedures. The manual also details the scope of delivery, required materials, and system documentation, which includes technical drawings, software tools, spare parts catalog, and certificates. The document emphasizes safety, proper handling, and maintenance of the analyzer system, with specific instructions for various components and operational scenarios.

structure.title: Preamble
structure.summary: The partial document provides an overview of the ACF5000 Installation Instructions, outlining the purpose and contents of the operator's manual. It details the system documentation included with the analyzer, such as data sheets, certificates, software tools, spare parts catalogs, and technical diagrams. It also includes information on accessing further support via the ABB website and contacting ABB service for assistance. Safety instructions are explained, with warnings, notes, and hazard classifications for potential risks. The intended use of the ACF5000 analyzer system is specified, emphasizing its role in continuous gas or vapor concentration measurement and prohibiting use in explosive environments or for measuring ignitable gas mixtures. The document also explains the formatting conventions used in the manual, such as reference numbers, display information, and user input methods.

structure.title: Safety instructions
structure.summary: The partial document provides safety instructions and operational guidelines for the ACF5000 analyzer system, emphasizing safe handling, installation, and operation. Key points include: safety requirements for personnel, adherence to safety regulations and standards (such as EN 61010), proper grounding procedures, and warnings about risks associated with opening equipment or working with hazardous gases. Specific safety measures are outlined for handling the analyzer system, including precautions for working with poisonous gases, hydrogen combustion gas paths, and the FTIR spectrometer. The document also describes the ACF5000 system's intended use for continuous measurement of gas concentrations in flue gas from industrial incinerators, its application in emissions monitoring and process control, and its operation based on FTIR spectrometry. The system includes a heated sample gas line, a gas sampling probe with a particulate filter, and a zirconium dioxide sensor for oxygen measurement.

nodes.title: Intended use
nodes.summary: The partial document outlines safety instructions and intended use for the ACF5000 analyzer system. It specifies that the device is designed for continuous measurement of gas or vapor components and must not be used for ignitable gas/air or gas/oxygen mixtures, nor in potentially explosive atmospheres. The document emphasizes proper handling, installation, operation, and maintenance, requiring qualified personnel familiar with similar devices. It highlights the importance of following the operator's manual, safety labels, and applicable regulations for electrical and gas handling. The device complies with EN 61010 Part 1 safety standards and must be grounded properly, with warnings about the risks of interrupting the protective conductor. Failure to follow these guidelines may endanger personnel and damage equipment.

nodes.title: Safety instructions
nodes.summary: The partial document outlines safety instructions for the operation, installation, and maintenance of a device, emphasizing the importance of proper handling, qualified personnel, and adherence to safety regulations. Key points include: requirements for safe operation, qualifications of personnel, observance of instructions and regulations (including national and international standards), device safety compliance with EN 61010 Part 1, proper grounding procedures, risks associated with interrupted grounding, hazards when opening equipment covers, and the need for trained personnel when working with live equipment. It also specifies conditions under which safe operation is no longer assured, such as visible damage or improper storage. Additionally, it highlights safety warnings for handling analyzer systems, including risks of electric shock, hot surfaces, and poisonous gases, and stresses the importance of not opening gas paths without subsequent leak testing.

nodes.title: Safety instructions for handling the analyzer system
nodes.summary: The partial document covers safety instructions for handling an analyzer system, emphasizing the importance of observing warning symbols and adhering to operating instructions. It highlights key hazards such as hot surfaces (>60°C), risk of electric shock, and the dangers associated with poisonous gases and FTIR spectrometers. Specific safety precautions are detailed for systems with an integral VOC analyzer, including the use of hydrogen flow restrictors, stainless steel piping, and proper shutoff procedures for hydrogen supply. It stresses the importance of not opening gas or combustion gas paths to prevent leaks, and mandates leak testing with a hydrogen leak detector if such paths are opened. The document also warns against removing or modifying safety components like bulkhead fittings and emphasizes regular inspection of gas paths to prevent fires and explosions.

nodes.title: Safety instructions for handling an analyzer system with integral VOC analyzer
nodes.summary: The partial document outlines safety instructions for the installation and operation of the ACF5000 analyzer system, focusing on two main components: the integral VOC analyzer and the FTIR spectrometer. Key points include safety precautions for handling hydrogen and combustion gas systems, such as using stainless steel piping, installing hydrogen flow restrictors and sintered metal fittings, and ensuring leak-free combustion gas paths. It emphasizes the importance of not opening the combustion gas path without a hydrogen leak test and warns against tampering with safety components. The document also describes the "hydrogen monitoring of the analyzer cabinet" option, which includes gas sensors, solenoid valves, and contactors to shut off hydrogen and power at 40% LEL to prevent explosions. Additionally, it covers electrical safety for the FTIR spectrometer, noting it is Safety Class 1 equipment, and includes laser safety guidelines for Class 3B VCSEL lasers, stressing the need for protective eyewear and restricting access to authorized personnel. The instructions highlight the risks of improper installation or operation, including fire, explosion, electric shock, and laser exposure.

nodes.title: Safety instructions for handling an FTIR spectrometer
nodes.summary: The partial document outlines safety instructions for the installation and operation of an FTIR spectrometer, covering electrical, laser, and hazardous gas safety. It emphasizes that the equipment is Safety Class 1 and must be properly grounded, with warnings against using incorrect fuses or operating damaged units. It highlights the risk of electric shock and fire, and warns against exposure to excessive moisture or explosive atmospheres. The document also addresses laser safety, noting the presence of a Class 3B VCSEL laser (760 nm, 2 mW) that is invisible and poses eye hazards; it stresses that the interferometer housing must not be opened by unauthorized personnel and that laser safety glasses are required when working on open components. Additionally, it addresses the handling of poisonous gases, requiring leak checks, proper ventilation, and safe discharge of diluted stack gas to prevent exposure to hazardous substances.

nodes.title: Safety instructions for working with poisonous gases
nodes.summary: The partial document covers safety instructions for working with poisonous gases and provides a description of the ACF5000 analyzer system. The safety section emphasizes the importance of preventing gas leaks, ensuring proper ventilation, and discharging diluted stack gas outside the analyzer room. It also highlights the need for regular leak checks and safe handling of hazardous gases. The description of the ACF5000 system outlines its application in continuous measurement of flue gas components in industrial incinerators, primarily for emissions monitoring but also suitable for process control. It details the system's function, including gas sampling via a heated line, filtration, automatic zero and test gas connection, and the use of an injector principle for gas conveyance. The system operates using FTIR spectrometry to measure gas concentrations based on infrared absorption, with additional integration of a zirconium dioxide sensor for oxygen measurement.

structure.title: Description of the ACF5000 analyzer system
structure.summary: The partial document provides an overview of the ACF5000 analyzer system, detailing its purpose, function, measuring principle, and components. It describes the system as a multi-component analyzer for continuous measurement of flue gas concentrations in industrial incinerators, primarily used for emissions monitoring but also applicable in process control. The system operates using FTIR spectrometry to measure various gas components based on infrared absorption, with a zirconium dioxide sensor for oxygen measurement. Key features include heated sample lines to prevent condensation, automatic zero and test gas connections, and optional components such as a validation wheel, flame ionization detector (FID) for total carbon (VOC) measurement, and remote monitoring via Ethernet or UMTS. The document also outlines the system's components, including the gas sampling probe, heated sample handling block, FTIR spectrometer, oxygen and VOC analyzers, and control unit with various interfaces. Additionally, it covers installation considerations, such as selecting a representative sampling point and ensuring accessibility for maintenance, in compliance with standards like DIN EN 15259.

nodes.title: Description of the analyzer system
nodes.summary: The partial document provides an overview of the ACF5000 analyzer system, detailing its application, function, measuring principle, options, and components. It describes the system as a multi-component analyzer for continuous measurement of flue gas concentrations in industrial incinerators, primarily used for emissions monitoring but also applicable in process control. The system draws gas via a heated sampling probe and line, with filtration and heating to prevent condensation. It uses FTIR spectrometry to measure various gas components based on infrared absorption, with a zirconium dioxide sensor for oxygen measurement. Optional features include a validation wheel, a flame ionization detector (FID) for total carbon (VOC) measurement, and remote monitoring via Ethernet or UMTS. The system includes components such as a gas sampling probe, heated sample handling block, FTIR spectrometer, oxygen and VOC analyzers, and an AO2000 system controller with various interfaces for data output and remote control. The document also notes that the system must use certified software for compliance with European emission directives.

nodes.title: Components of the analyzer system
nodes.summary: The partial document provides installation instructions for the ACF5000 analyzer system, detailing its components, including gas sampling equipment (such as probe tubes, filter units, and heated sample lines), sample gas handling systems (like the ASP block and sensors), air purifiers, and analyzers (FTIR spectrometer, oxygen analyzer, and optional VOC analyzer). It also describes control and display components, including the AO2000 system controller, interfaces for data output and remote control, and software requirements for compliance with European Directives. Additionally, it outlines preparation steps for installation, focusing on selecting a representative sampling point, ensuring accessibility for maintenance, and protecting the filter unit, with reference to standards such as DIN EN 15259 and DIN EN ISO/IEC 17025.

structure.title: Preparing for installation
structure.summary: The partial document provides detailed instructions for preparing for the installation of the ACF5000 gas analyzer system. It covers the selection and installation of the sampling point and wall tube, including specifications for mounting flanges, gaskets, and alignment considerations. It outlines requirements for the analyzer cabinet installation site, emphasizing safety from explosive atmospheres, protection from environmental factors, and climatic conditions. The document specifies space requirements, floor strength, and altitude limitations affecting gas flow and system performance. It details sample gas inlet conditions, including temperature, pressure, and flow rate, and specifies requirements for process and test gases for various analyzers (FTIR, VOC, O₂). The power supply specifications include voltage, frequency, fuse ratings, and power consumption for different components. It lists the scope of delivery, materials required for installation (not supplied), and cable specifications for signal and power connections. The document also includes information on dimensions, weights, noise levels, and general installation recommendations, emphasizing adherence to safety standards and proper handling of equipment.

nodes.title: Selection of the sampling point, installation of the wall tube
nodes.summary: The partial document covers preparation steps for the installation of a gas analysis system, focusing on the selection of the sampling point, installation of the wall tube with mounting flange, and requirements for the analyzer cabinet installation site. Key points include ensuring the sampling point allows for a representative sample and easy maintenance, protecting the PFE2 filter unit with an IP54 enclosure, and adhering to DIN EN 15259 standards. It provides detailed instructions for installing the wall tube in various structures (brickwork, metal sheeting, insulated channels), including dimensions and flow direction. The document also specifies minimum distances based on installation angle and emphasizes the importance of short gas paths to reduce dead times, with limits on heated sample line lengths depending on voltage. Safety warnings include avoiding explosive atmospheres, and environmental protection requirements such as shielding from water, chemicals, sunlight, dust, vibration, and corrosive conditions. Climatic conditions for storage, transport, and operation are outlined, including temperature and humidity ranges, with notes on optional features like built-in fans or air conditioners and the need for proper packaging during transport.

nodes.title: Requirements for the analyzer cabinet installation site
nodes.summary: The partial document outlines the preparation requirements for installing an analyzer cabinet, focusing on site selection, environmental conditions, and operational specifications. Key points include: the analyzer cabinet must not be installed in potentially explosive atmospheres; short gas paths are essential to minimize dead times, with maximum line lengths of 60 meters (230 V AC) or 40 meters (120 V AC); the cabinet must be protected from water, chemicals, sunlight, air currents, dust, corrosion, and vibration; climatic conditions specify ambient temperatures for storage, transport, and operation, with options for built-in fan or air conditioner; the installation site must be indoors, with a maximum altitude of 800 m above sea level, and a minimum inlet pressure of 900 hPa to ensure proper system function; space requirements include 0.5 m on the right and left, 1 m at the front, and 0.5 m above for air conditioning; the floor must be level and strong enough to support the cabinet's weight (approx. 300 kg); the analyzer system cannot measure ignitable gas mixtures or gases containing organometallic compounds like lead or silicone oils; for HF measurement, FFKM seals are required; and sample gas inlet conditions include a controlled temperature of 180 ± 2 °C, inlet pressure of 900–1100 hPa, and a flow rate of approximately 200–250 L/h.

nodes.title: Sample gas inlet conditions
nodes.summary: The partial document outlines preparation requirements for the installation of an analyzer system, focusing on sample gas inlet conditions and process/test gas specifications. It specifies that for HF measurement, FFKM seals are required. The document details temperature control (180 ± 2 °C), inlet pressure (900–1100 hPa), and flow rate (200–250 L/h) for the sample gas. It also provides specifications for the FTIR spectrometer and VOC analyzer, including required gas types (zero, span, combustion), their quality, inlet pressures, and flow rates. Additional notes explain gas generation methods and conversion requirements for VOC analyzer calibration.

nodes.title: Power supply

structure.title: Installation
structure.summary: The partial document provides detailed installation instructions for the ACF5000 analyzer system, covering general installation guidelines, setup of the analyzer cabinet, unpacking and handling procedures, installation of components such as the analysis cabinet, gas sampling probe, filter unit, sample gas lines, operating gases, and electrical connections. nodes.title: General information
nodes.summary: The partial document provides installation instructions for the ACF5000 analyzer system, emphasizing that installation should ideally be performed by ABB. It highlights the importance of referring to the operator's manual, order-specific drawings, and technical documentation for individual components. It also advises on handling shipping damage by filing a claim within seven days and ensuring all accessories are accounted for. The document recommends retaining packaging materials for future transport and stresses that the analyzer cabinet should be transported lying on its back and only stood up just before installation. Additionally, it outlines the need for a proper foundation, referencing site requirements and a location diagram, and specifies the use of a concrete base with M10 stud bolts or an iron base frame with appropriate dimensions.

nodes.title: Setting up the analyzer cabinet
nodes.summary: The partial document covers the installation procedures for an ACF5000 analyzer cabinet, including transportation, unpacking, and setup. Key points include: recommendations for transporting the cabinet on its back and standing it up only before installation; requirements for the foundation, such as a concrete base with M10 stud bolts or an iron base frame; and the need for a crane due to the cabinet's weight (approx. 300 kg). Unpacking instructions emphasize using transport lugs and ensuring a minimum 45° angle for pull ropes to prevent warping, and advise against removing the protective plastic film until the cabinet reaches room temperature (after at least 24 hours). Installation steps include observing site requirements, using earthing via a central screw, and routing the earthing cable through a provided M16 cable gland. The document also details removing transport securing devices from the ASP block using a 13 mm spanner, and installing optional components such as the electrical distributor cabinet, heated 3/2-way solenoid valve, and gas sampling probe with filter unit. Specific attention is given to connecting sample gas lines, following the piping and wiring diagrams, and assembling the probe with its protective case, including mounting angles and dimensions.

nodes.title: Installing the gas sampling probe and filter unit
nodes.summary:
The partial document covers the installation procedures for a gas sampling system, focusing on the installation of the gas sampling probe and filter unit, as well as the sample gas line. Key points include:  
- Instructions for installing the pre-assembled probe tube with filter unit, noting that two people are required due to the weight (17–32 kg), and referencing the piping, wiring, and terminal diagrams.  
- Specific steps for different probe types (type 40 and type 42), including insertion into the wall tube, flange connection, and electrical wiring.  
- Details on assembling the protective case with the PFE2 filter unit, including mounting angles and dimensions.  
- Specifications for probe tube types, including materials (Edelstahl W-Nr. 1.4571), lengths, and dimensions.  
- Guidance on connecting electrical leads and ensuring proper insulation and heating for the heated probe tube to maintain operating temperature.  
- Instructions for installing the sample gas line, emphasizing the avoidance of grease, sharp bends, kinks, and water pockets, and ensuring a minimum bending radius of 200 mm.  
- Requirements for laying the heated sample gas line, including avoiding walls with sealing compounds, cable channels, and proximity to other gas or power lines.  
- Instructions for assembling heated sample gas lines on C-profiles and inserting the line into the analysis cabinet.

nodes.title: Installing the sample gas line
nodes.summary: The partial document provides detailed instructions for installing various gas lines and components in a system, focusing on the proper setup of sample gas lines, operating gas supplies, and test gas cylinders. Key points include: connecting the sample gas line to the gas sampling probe while avoiding grease or lubricants, ensuring proper inclination and routing to prevent water pockets, avoiding sharp bends and crossings with other lines, and using heated sample gas lines correctly. It emphasizes safety and accuracy by prohibiting certain installation practices (e.g., sealing compounds, cable channels) and specifying the use of PTFE tubes and blanking plugs. The document also covers connecting electrical leads, installing instrument air and test gas lines, ensuring cleanliness during connections, and installing combustion gas lines with safety features like flow limiters. It references system documentation, including piping, wiring, and terminal diagrams, and highlights that certain connections are to be made by ABB personnel during commissioning.

nodes.title: Installing the operating gases
nodes.summary: The partial document outlines the installation procedures for an ACF5000 analyzer system, covering the installation of operating gases, instrument air supply, test gas cylinders, gas lines, combustion gas, waste gas, purge gas, and electrical connections. Key points include observing safety and regulatory requirements, using specified materials and diagrams (e.g., piping, arrangement, wiring, and terminal diagrams), ensuring cleanliness and proper sealing of gas lines, installing shut-off devices and pressure gauges, connecting gas and electrical lines with attention to separation and shielding, and verifying seal integrity using a hydrogen leak detector. Special attention is given to safety components like flow limiters and protective earth connections, as well as compliance with national regulations for pressure vessels and electrical systems.

nodes.title: Connecting the electrical leads
nodes.summary: The partial document covers the installation and commissioning procedures for an analyzer system. Key points include connecting electrical leads, ensuring compliance with safety regulations, and properly laying signal and power supply lines. It emphasizes separating signal lines from power lines, using terminal blocks for connections, and adhering to local regulations for screened cables. The power supply section highlights high leakage current and the importance of matching voltage settings and securing protective earth connections. The commissioning process involves restarting the system after shutdown, activating power and instrument air, checking pressures, and ensuring proper heating of components. It also includes steps for connecting sample gas lines, conducting a seal integrity test, and restarting the hydrogen supply and FID. Safety warnings and procedural steps are clearly outlined.

structure.title: Commissioning
structure.summary: The partial document covers the commissioning and restart procedures for the ACF5000 analyzer system, including steps for powering up the system, activating circuit breakers, feeding instrument air, and ensuring proper pressure and temperature conditions. It emphasizes safety precautions, such as keeping the hydrogen supply off during initial startup and conducting a seal integrity test. The document also outlines the automatic start of measurements by the oxygen sensor, FTIR spectrometer, and FID after restart. Additionally, it includes a section on inspection and maintenance, specifying that only qualified personnel should perform maintenance and that various safety instructions must be followed.

nodes.title: Restart
nodes.summary: The partial document covers the commissioning and restart procedures for the ACF5000 analyzer system, including steps for powering up the system, activating circuit breakers, feeding instrument air, and ensuring proper pressure and temperature conditions. structure.title: Inspection and maintenance
structure.summary: The partial document provides detailed instructions for the inspection, maintenance, and replacement of components in the ACF5000 analyzer system. Key points include safety precautions for qualified personnel, visual inspection of the analysis cabinet and instrument components, cleaning procedures, and seal integrity testing (both complete and simplified methods). It outlines specific procedures for testing the seal integrity of various gas paths using oxygen measurement and FID methods, as well as checking combustion gas paths with a hydrogen leak detector. The document also details the replacement of wearing parts such as filters, batteries, and O-rings, including step-by-step instructions for replacing filters on the gas sampling probe, in the ASP block, in the compressed air regulator, and in the fan, along with safety warnings and precautions. Additionally, it covers the shutdown and packing of the analyzer system for temporary or long-term storage.

nodes.title: Visual inspection
nodes.summary: The partial document covers inspection and maintenance procedures for an ACF5000 analysis cabinet, focusing on visual inspection of external and internal components, including instrument air regulators, gas cylinder pressure reducers, and various pressure settings for different systems (e.g., combustion air, VOC analyzer, purge air). It details the status of indicators such as display readings, purge gas flow, filter pads, status LEDs, cooling unit display, and circuit breakers. Additionally, it provides cleaning instructions, emphasizing the use of dry methods like brushing and vacuuming to avoid moisture or solvents, and specifies safe cleaning practices for the cabinet exterior while ensuring the door remains closed during operation.

nodes.title: Cleaning instructions
nodes.summary: The partial document covers cleaning instructions and seal integrity testing procedures for an analysis cabinet and analyzer system. It includes guidelines for cleaning the interior and exterior of the cabinet, emphasizing the use of dry methods and avoiding water or solvents. It also details two types of seal integrity tests: a complete test performed by certified personnel at least annually or after system maintenance, and a simplified test used after specific maintenance tasks such as replacing the gas sampling probe, sample gas line, or filter. The simplified tests include methods using oxygen measurement and a flame ionization detector (FID) with a hydrocarbon source to detect leaks in the sample gas path. The document stresses that the simplified test is not a substitute for the complete test.

nodes.title: Seal integrity test
nodes.summary: The partial document outlines the installation and maintenance procedures for the ACF5000 analyzer system, focusing on seal integrity testing and replacement of wearing parts. It details two types of seal integrity tests: the complete test, which is reserved for certified service personnel and must be performed annually or after system modifications, and the simplified test, which is used for specific scenarios such as after replacing components like the gas sampling probe or sample gas filter. The simplified tests include methods using oxygen measurement and a flame ionization detector (FID) with a felt pen or gas lighter to detect leaks. The document also specifies procedures for checking the combustion gas path seal using a hydrogen leak detector and lists indicators of potential leaks, such as abnormal pressure readings or oxygen concentrations. Additionally, it provides a schedule for replacing wearing parts, including filters, batteries, and other components, with recommended replacement cycles based on environmental conditions. It emphasizes the use of genuine ABB spare parts and directs users to an online parts ordering system.

nodes.title: Replacing wearing parts
nodes.summary: The partial document provides installation and maintenance instructions for the ACF5000 analyzer system, focusing on replacing wearing parts and ensuring proper system operation during maintenance. Key points include: activating the maintenance controller and setting gas flow control to prevent contact with sample gas before maintenance; resetting controls after maintenance; a detailed replacement cycle for various filters and components (e.g., gas sampling probe filter, ASP block filter, compressed air regulator filter, fan filter, and battery) based on dust content; use of genuine ABB spare parts only; and specific instructions for replacing the gas sampling probe filter, including the use of FFKM seals and part numbers. It also mentions the availability of spare parts information online and the option to replace the entire filter insert to minimize system downtime.

nodes.title: Replacing filters on the gas sampling probe
nodes.summary: The partial document provides detailed instructions for the inspection, maintenance, and replacement of filters in a gas sampling system, specifically for the ACF5000 analyzer. It covers the replacement of wearing parts such as stainless steel filters and FFKM seals, emphasizing the use of specific item numbers and proper handling procedures. The document outlines steps for replacing the entire filter insert and cleaning or replacing the filter element, including safety precautions like wearing protective gloves and goggles due to high temperatures and potential exposure to hazardous gases. It also includes procedures for removing and reinstalling the filter unit, ensuring seal integrity, and restoring the system to normal operation. Additionally, it addresses the replacement of the sample gas filter in the ASP block, highlighting the need for grease-free tools and materials to prevent contamination, especially in systems with integrated FID. The instructions are structured to minimize system downtime and ensure accurate measurements by maintaining cleanliness and proper assembly.

nodes.title: Replacing sample gas filter in the ASP block
nodes.summary: The partial document provides detailed instructions for the inspection and maintenance of sample gas filters in the ASP block and the compressed air main regulator of an ACF5000 analyzer system. It covers the replacement of wearing parts, specifically the sample gas filter (item no. 0768914) and the filter in the compressed air main regulator (item no. 990048), with recommended replacement intervals based on dust content. The document emphasizes safety precautions, such as wearing protective gloves and goggles due to high temperatures and potential hydrocarbon contamination. It outlines step-by-step procedures for removing, cleaning, or replacing filters, including preparing the system by interrupting measuring mode, using degreased tools, and ensuring proper O-ring placement. It also includes instructions for fitting new filters, tightening components, and restoring normal operation, including performing a seal integrity test. The text highlights the importance of using new O-rings and avoiding contamination to maintain measurement accuracy.

nodes.title: Replacing filter in the compressed air main regulator (-J85)
nodes.summary: The partial document provides detailed instructions for inspecting and maintaining the ACF5000 analyzer system, focusing on replacing filters in two key components: the compressed air main regulator (-J85) and the sample gas pressure regulator. It outlines the necessary steps for safely replacing the filter elements, including preparing the system by interrupting measuring mode, relieving pressure, and ensuring proper reassembly. The document also lists wearing parts with their item numbers and recommended replacement intervals based on ambient dust levels. Safety precautions, such as handling pressurized systems and using appropriate tools, are emphasized throughout the procedures.

nodes.title: Replacing filters in the sample gas pressure regulator
nodes.summary: The partial document covers maintenance procedures for replacing wearing parts in the ACF5000 system. It includes instructions for replacing the filter in the sample gas pressure regulator and the filter pad in the fan. For the sample gas pressure regulator, the filter (item no. 4805885) should be replaced every 6–12 months depending on ambient dust levels, involving removal of the ACF5000-E-Box cover, replacing the paper filter, and reassembling. For the fan, the filter pad (item no. 990046) also requires replacement every 6–12 months, with steps to remove the fan grille, replace the filter pad, and reinsert the grille at both the inlet and outlet filters. The document emphasizes routine maintenance to ensure proper system operation.

nodes.title: Replacing filter pad in the fan
nodes.summary: The partial document provides installation and maintenance instructions for the ACF5000 system, focusing on replacing wearing parts. It details the replacement of the filter pad in the inlet and outlet filters, which should be done every 6–12 months depending on ambient dust levels, including steps for removing and reinstalling the fan grille. It also covers replacing backup batteries in the system controller and ACF5000-E-Box, specifying battery types (Varta CR3032 or Renata CR2032) and a replacement interval of approximately every 4 years. Safety precautions are emphasized, particularly the risk of electrostatic discharge when handling electronic components, with instructions to disconnect power before battery replacement. The document includes step-by-step procedures for battery replacement and proper disposal of used batteries.

nodes.title: Replacing back-up batteries
nodes.summary: The partial document covers maintenance procedures for replacing backup batteries in an analyzer system, specifically focusing on the system controller and the ACF5000-E-Box. It details the types of batteries used (Varta CR3032 or Renata CR2032), their replacement intervals (approximately every 4 years), and step-by-step instructions for safely replacing them, emphasizing precautions against electrostatic discharge and proper disposal of used batteries. Additionally, it includes instructions for shutting down and packing the analyzer system, covering steps such as switching gas flow controls, disconnecting sample lines, turning off power supplies, and shutting off instrument air.

structure.title: Shutting down and packing the analyzer system
structure.summary: The partial document covers the procedures for shutting down and packing the ACF5000 analyzer system. It includes detailed steps for temporarily shutting down the system, such as switching gas flow controls, disconnecting sample lines, and turning off power and instrument air. It also outlines the packing process, including vacuum packing the analysis cabinet, using desiccant, placing the cabinet in a transport crate with snubbers and chocks, and marking the crate as fragile. Additional notes emphasize the importance of dry and heated packing conditions, avoiding moisture, and proper transport and storage conditions. The document also includes an index listing various topics covered in the manual, such as installation, safety instructions, maintenance, and commissioning.

nodes.title: Shutting down the analyzer system
nodes.summary: The partial document covers the procedures for shutting down and packing an analyzer system, specifically the ACF5000 model. It includes steps for temporarily shutting down the system, such as switching gas flow controls to zero gas modes, disconnecting sample lines, and turning off power and instrument air. It also details the packing process, including vacuum-packing the cabinet, using desiccant, placing it in a transport crate with snubbers, and marking the crate as fragile. Additional notes emphasize the importance of dry and heated packing conditions, avoiding moisture, and adhering to specified transport and storage environmental conditions (temperature: –25 to +65 °C, humidity ≤ 75%). The document recommends using a specialist transport company and transporting the cabinet horizontally on its rear.

nodes.title: Packing the analysis cabinet
nodes.summary: The partial document provides installation instructions for the ACF5000 analyzer system, focusing on the packing of the analysis cabinet for transport. Key points include vacuum-packing the cabinet, using appropriate desiccant, placing the cabinet on snubbers and chocks in a transport crate, and marking the crate as "Fragile product." It emphasizes the importance of dry and heated packing conditions, avoiding moisture that could freeze, and recommends using a specialist transport company. The cabinet must be transported horizontally on its rear. Ambient transport and storage conditions are specified (temperature: –25 to +65 °C, humidity ≤ 75%). The document also includes a detailed index listing sections such as cleaning, commissioning, installation, safety instructions, maintenance, and troubleshooting, indicating a comprehensive guide covering all aspects of the analyzer system's setup, operation, and upkeep.

6 ACF5000 Installation Instructions  
 
Safety instructions 
 
 
Intended use  
Intended use 
The ACF5000 analyzer system is designed for continuous measurement 
of the concentration of individual components in gases or vapors.  
Any other application is not compliant with the specified use.  
Intended use also includes taking note of this operator's manual.  
The analyzer system may not be used for the measurement of ignitable gas/air or gas/oxygen mixtures during normal service. The analyzer sy s-
tem may not be set up in potentially explosive atmospheres.  
In normal service, the interior of the analyzer system  contains no poten-
tially explosive atmosphere. Accordingly, installation of explosion protec-tion in the interior is not necessary for operation of the analyzer system.

Safety  instructions  7 
 
Safety instructions 
Requirements for safe operation 
In order  to operate in a safe and efficient manner, the device should be 
properly handled and stored, correctly installed and set up, properly op-
erated and correctly maintained.  
Qualifications of the personnel  
Only persons familiar with the installation, commissio ning, operation and 
maintenance of comparable devices and certified as being capable of such work should work on the device.  
Instructions and regulations to be observed 
These include 
• The contents of this operator's manual,  
• The safety information affixed to the device,  
• The applicable safety regulations for installing and operating electrical 
devices as well as  
• The applicable safety regulations for working with gases, acids, con-
densates, etc.  
National regulations 
The regulations and norms, standards and direc tives cited in this oper a-
tor's manual are applicable in the Federal Republic of Germany. The ap-plicable national regulations should be followed when the device is used in other countries.  
Device safety and safe operation 
The device has been designed and tested in accordance with EN 61010 Part 1, "Safety requirements for electrical equipment for measurement, 
control, and laboratory use" and has been shipped ready for safe oper a-
tion. 
In order to maintain this condition and to assure safe operation, the safety  
information in this operator's manual must be observed. Failure to do so 
can put personnel at risk and lead to equipment damage as well as dam-age to other systems and devices.  
Protective conductor terminal  
The protective conductor (grounding wire) should be attached to the pr o-
tective conductor terminal before any other connection is made.  
Risk when the equipment grounding conductor is interrupted 
The unit can pose a danger if the protective conductor (equipment 
grounding conductor) is interrupted inside or  outside the unit or is discon-
nected from the protective conductor terminal.

8 ACF5000 Installation Instructions  
 
Risks involved when opening the covers  
Current -conducting components can be exposed when the covers or 
parts are removed, even if this can be done without tools. Current can be 
present at some connection points.  
Risks involved in working with open equipment  
All work on equipment that is open and connected to power should be 
performed only by trained personnel who are familiar with the risks i n-
volved.  
When safe operation can no longer be assured …  
If it is apparent that safe operation is no longer possible, the device 
should be taken out of operation and secured against unauthorized use.  
The possibility of safe operation is excluded:  
• If the device is visibly damaged,  
• If the device no longer operates,  
• After prolonged storage under adverse conditions,  
• After severe transport stresses.

Safety  instructions  9 
 
Safety instructions for handling the analyzer system  
 The warning symbols affixed to the analyzer system must be observed“”:  
 
 Heed the operating instructions!  
 
 Hot surface! (Temperature >  60 °C) 
 
 Risk of electric shock!  
 The following must also be observed:  
• The safety instructions for handling an analyzer system with integral 
VOC analyzer  (see page  10) 
• The safety instructions for working with poisonous gases  (see page 
13)  
• The safety instructions fo r handling an FTIR spectrometer  (see page 
12) 
 
 The gas paths in the analyzer system and the integral analyzer must not 
be opened! The gas paths can become leaky as a result ! 
If the gas paths inside the analyzer system must nevertheless be opened, 
it is essential that they be subjected to a leak test after being closed 
again.

10 ACF5000 Installation Instructions  
 
Safety instru ctions for handling an analyzer system with integral 
VOC analyzer  
Safety precautions 
If a VOC analyzer is installed in the analyzer system, the following safety 
precautions must be taken at the factory to ensure safe operation:  
• Installation of a hydrogen f low restrictor in the cabinet wall (bulkhead 
fitting with an integrated flow restrictor, max.  10 L/h, for connection to 
the combustion gas line),  
• Use of stainless steel piping, compression fittings and valves,  
• Shutoff of the hydrogen supply in the event of  malfunctions,  
• Check of the combustion gas paths for leaks inside the analyzer ca b-
inet, 
• Installation of a sintered metal fitting in the cabinet wall to allow e s-
cape of hydrogen to the outside in the event of leaks.  
 
 The combustion gas path in the analyze r cabinet and especially in the 
integral VOC analyzer must not be opened! The combustion gas path can 
become leaky as a result!  
If the combustion gas path inside the analyzer cabinet must nevertheless 
be opened, it is essential that it be subjected to a leak test with a hydr o-
gen leak detector (thermal conductivity) after it is closed again!  
 The bulkhead fitting with integral flow restrictor for connection of the com-
bustion gas line is a safety -relevant component. It must not be removed, 
modified or replac ed under any circumstances!  
The integrity of the combustion gas path in the analyzer system as well as 
the combustion gas feed line must be checked prior to commissioning as well as regularly during operation.  
 Combustion gas that escapes from leaks in the gas paths can cause fires and explosions, even outside the analyzer system!

Safety  instructions  11 
 
"Hydrogen monitoring of the analyzer cabinet" option 
Function  
The "hydrogen monitoring of the analyzer cabinet" option is an additional 
safety measure. If a leak occurs in the h ydrogen path inside the analyzer 
cabinet and hydrogen accumulates inside the cabinet, both the hydrogen 
supply and the power are shut off before the explosion limit is reached – 
at 40 % LEL. This prevents formation of an ignitable mixture.  
Scope of deliver y 
Installed in the analyzer cabinet:  
• In the upper area, an ATEX -certified gas sensor with connection 
socket,  
• On the sidewall, a solenoid valve that interrupts the hydrogen supply at 40% LEL.  
Also supplied:  
• A gas warning center for evaluating the gas sensor  signal,  
• A contactor for disconnecting the power supply to the analyzer cabi-net, 
• A contactor for disconnecting the UPS if the system is prepared for a 
UPS.  
Installation  
The gas warning center must be installed outside the analyzer cabinet 
in a non- hazardou s area in a distribution cabinet or the like. It must be 
electrically connected to the gas sensor (see the project -specific dra w-
ings in this regard). Operation and signal evaluation are the responsibility 
of the user; they are independent of the analyzer s ystem.  
The solenoid valve  for disconnecting the hydrogen supply as well as the 
coils of the contactors and relays for disconnecting the power supply and 
UPS (if present) must be connected to a fault -signaling contact in the gas 
warning center. The fault -signaling contact must be set so that the voltage 
is shut off at 40% LEL and the contact itself latches.  
The measuring signals (analog outputs and inputs), the status signals 
(digital outputs and inputs) as well as the bus systems of the analyzer 
system are so designed that after the power supply (and possibly the 
UPS) are disconnected no component in the analyzer cabinet (contactor, 
relay, motor etc.) that could generate an ignition spark can be actuated 
from the outside.  
In the factory -supplied state, the m easuring and status signals as well as 
the bus systems do not need to be shut off in the event of an alarm. If, 
however, an additional external signal is fed in, it is necessary to check 
whether this signal must be shut off when the gas sensor indicates a 
fault.  
 
 If the above- mentioned instructions are not observed or the option is i n-
stalled incorrectly, a hydrogen explosion may occur in the event of a mal-
function.

12 ACF5000 Installation Instructions  
 
Safety instructions for handli ng an FTIR spectrometer  
Electrical safety  
The FTIR spectrometer has an unprotected metal housing that is co n-
nected directly to ground potential via the power cable and is thus class i-
fied as "Safety Class  1 Equipment".  
 
 Before fuses are replaced, the unit  must be disconnected from the power 
supply.  
To avoid electric shock, the unit may not be operated if there is an indic a-
tion that any part of the outer surface is damaged.  
 To protect against fires, only a fuse of the specified type and current rating 
may be used.  
To protect against electric shock, the protective conductor (equipment 
grounding conductor) of the power cable must be connected to ground 
potential.  
WARNING! The unit must not be exposed to any source of the excessive moisture.  
The unit may not be used in an explosive hazardous atmosphere.  
NOTE  Approval from the responsible authorities is required for measurement of 
combustible gases.  
Laser safety  
Under normal conditions, the FTIR spectrometer can be operated com-
pletely safely (Class 1 laser product – see name plate).  
 
 Type of laser installed in the interferometer: Class  3B VCSEL laser to 
IEC 60825 -1 as well as 21 CFR Chapter  1, Subchapter  J  
Output: max.  2 mW  
Wavelengt h: 760 nm (laser beam invisible to the human eye)  
 The housing of the interferometer may not be opened during normal op-
eration. It contains no user -operated parts.  
The housing of the interferometer may be opened only by authorized ABB 
service personnel.  
Opening the housing of the interferometer and the interferometer module 
in particular can result in contact with laser radiation.  
Radiation from Class 3B lasers poses a danger to the human eye both 
when viewed directly or if reflected.  
When working on an open interferometer, it is absolutely essential to wear 
safety glasses that protect against laser radiation!

Safety  instructions  13 
 
Safety instructions for working with poisonous gases  
 Some gas components w hose concentration is measured with the ana-
lyzer system are hazardous to health or poisonous.  
For this reason, the sample gas must under no circumstances be allowed 
to escape from the sample gas path in either the measurement mode or 
when performing maintenance.  
The analyzer system must be checked for leaks regularly.  
The diluted stack gas must be discharged outside the room where the analyzer cabinet is installed.  
Ensure adequate ventilation of the room in which the analyzer system is 
installed.

14 ACF5000 Installation Instructions  
 
Description of the ACF5000 analyzer system  
 
 
Description of the analyzer system  
Application 
The ACF5000 analyzer system is a multi -component analyzer system  for 
continuous measurement of the concentration of individual components 
in the flue gas of industrial incinerators.  
The field of application of this measuring equipment basically involves 
tasks associated with emissions monitoring; use in process control appl i-
cations, h owever, is also possible.  
Function 
The gas to be measured is drawn from the gas channel by means of a 
gas sampling probe and conveyed to the analyzer cabinet via a heated 
sample gas line. The sampling probe contains a particulate filter that r e-
moves dust p articles from the gas. As a standard feature, the analyzer 
system controller offers the ability to connect the zero gas and test gas to the sampling probe upstream of the filter element automatically. Automat-ic cleaning of the sampling probe filter is avai lable as an option.  
The gas path from the sampling location to the analyzer is heated throughout (180 °C) to prevent the temperature from dropping below the 
dew point or condensation of flue gas. The heating is controlled and mon-
itored by the system's elec tronics.  
An optional heated measuring point selector can be configured for pr o-
cess measurements.  
Conveying of the sample to the analyzer is based on the injector principle 
and employs an air jet injector that is integrated into the heated sample 
handling block (ASP block). This, in turn, is connected directly to the 
heated gas cell.  
Test gases can be connected either automatically or manually to both the gas sampling probe and directly to the analyzer.  
Measuring principle  
The analyzer system operates on the principle of FTIR spectrometry. The 
concentrations of a variety of stack gas components that exhibit absor p-
tion bands in the mid- infrared range can be determined.  
Each gas absorbs infrared radiation in a specific region of the spectrum. 
The radiation absorbed at a given wavelength is a function of the gas 
concentration. The FTIR analyzer (spectrometer) measures how much 
radiation was absorbed at specific wavelengths.  
The information about the absorption processes is processed in the sy s-
tem's electronics and converted into measured values. At the same time, the spectra of all components are recorded.  
A zirconium dioxide sensor for measurement of the oxygen content is an 
integral part of the analyzer system.

Description  of the ACF5000 analyzer system  15 
 
Options  
Validation  
A validation wheel can be instal led in the beam path of the spectrometer 
to confirm the validity of the spectrometer adjustment.  
Total carbon measurement  
A flame ionization detector (FID) for measurement of the total carbon 
content (VOC) can be incorporated into the analyzer system.  
Disp lay and signal processing  
The current concentration of the individual measured components and 
the status signals are shown on the system display.  
The system controller has been designed for the requirements of emi s-
sions and process measurement. It offers a system -internal CAN bus and 
field bus systems such as Modbus and PROFIBUS as interfaces. An Ethernet interface for remote monitoring of the entire analyzer system and transmitting data via internal or external TCP/IP networks is included. 
Remote control of the analyzer system is possible via a UMTS router. 
Analog outputs for the measured components and relay contacts for fault/status messages are standard.

Requirements for the analyzer cabinet installation site  
WARNING! The analyzer cabinet may not be set up in pot entially explosive atmos-
pheres!  
Short gas paths  
• The analyzer cabinet should be set up as close as possible to the 
measuring point. A short sample gas line translates into short dead 
times. Because of the pressure drop in the line and the required ele c-
trical protection, the length of the heated sample gas line must not 
exceed 60 meters when connected to 230 V AC and 40 meters when 
connected to 120 V AC. Depending on the altitude of the installation 
site, these values may be lower.  
• The test gas bottles should be set up as close as possible to the ana-
lyzer cabinet.  
Protection from adverse conditions  
• The analyzer cabinet must be protected from  
• Jets of water,  
• Contact with chemicals,  
• Strong sunlight and heat,  
• Strong air currents,  
• Extremely dusty environments,  
• Corrosive atmospheres,  
• Vibration.

20 ACF5000 Installation Instructions  
 
Installation site  
The gas analyzer is intended solely for installation indoors.  
The maximum altitude of the installation site is 800 m above sea level (for 
10 m longer sample gas line with probe).  
Note: The minimum inlet pressure at the analyzer cabinet is 900 hPa. 
This yields a maximum elevation of the installation site of 800 m; howe v-
er, the pressure drop across the gas sampling probe (15 hPa for a new 
and clean probe) and the sample gas line must be taken into account. 
Higher altitudes would result in insufficient gas flow through the system. 
The inlet pressures for the ACF5000 may not be lowered, as this directly reduces the sensitivity of the FTIR spectrometer. As a consequence, the

Seal integrity test 
Complete seal integrity test of the analyzer system  
Complete seal integr ity tests of the analyzer system  are reserved for ce r-
tified service personnel.  
These tests must be performed regularly, at least once per year.  
They must be performed after gas paths within the system have been 
opened and following a restart from cold.  
Simplified seal integrity test of the sample gas path 
 
NOTE  The simplified seal integrity test is not suitable for testing the overall ana-
lyzer system  for seal integrity. Therefore, it cannot replace the regular 
complete seal integrity test in particular (see above).  
When must the simplified seal integrity test be performed?  
A simplified seal integrity test must be performed in the following cases:  
• Following work on the gas sampling probe (e.g. filter replacement),  
• following replacement of the sample gas line,  
• following replacement of the sample gas filter in the ASP block.  
The simplified seal integrity test serves to check the seal integrity of the 
analyzer system , from the gas sampling probe to the ASP block.  
Simplified seal integrity test via oxygen measure ment  
This method is based on connecting oxygen and observing the oxygen measured value.  
1 Feed -in nitrogen, either locally or via the gas sampling probe.  
2 Observe the oxygen measured value. After a running -in time of a p-
prox. 5 minutes with local feed- in or 2 0 minutes with feed in via the 
gas sampling probe, the oxygen measured value should drop to ap-prox. 0.08 %. 
3 Failure to do so indicates a leak in the selected gas path (see the 
pneumatic diagram in the order -related drawings).  
Simplified seal integrity test  via FID  
This method can be employed only if a FID is built into the analyzer sy s-
tem. It is based on allowing hydrocarbon to act on any leaking points in 
the sample gas path and observing the measured value on the FID at the same time. A commercially avail able felt pen is used as a punctiform "H y-
drocarbon source" for this purpose.  
1 Starting at the sample gas sampling probe and working towards the analysis cabinet, hold the felt pen briefly (1– 2 seconds) against each 
fitting, connection and screw.  
2 Observe the FID measured value. In the presence of a leak, the measured value rises and drops back to the normal value relatively 
quickly. Due to the calibration times, the measured value can rise af-
ter a delay; after each contact with the felt pen, wait at least 2 minutes 
for a possible reaction.

Inspection  and maintenance  49 
 
3 Open the cover of the ASP block and hold the felt pen briefly against 
the sample gas line connection at the ASP block.  
 
 The ASP block is hot (approx. 180 °C)! 
Wear suitable protective gloves and safety goggles!  
Note: A v ariant of this method is using a commercially available gas light-
er, which normally contains a propane -butane mixture, instead of the felt 
pen. Instead of holding the felt pen at the fittings etc., allow a small amount of lighter gas (no flame) to flow at the point being tested. Howe v-
er, this variant is significantly more non -selective for localizing a leak.  
Seal integrity test of the combustion gas path in the analyzer system  with VOC 
analyzer (FID)  
The seal integrity of the combustion gas line within the analyzer system  
must be checked on a regular basis (at least every 6 months) using a 
hydrogen leak detector (leak rate <  2 × 10–4 hPa l/s). Do not use leak 
detector spray!  
It is advisable to also check the seal integrity of the combustion gas line 
outside the analyzer system  on a regular basis.  
Other indications of leaks 
The following states can indicate a leak in the analyzer  system : 
• The SMI and SGO pressures to be regulated by the analyzer system  
are no longer reached.  
• The controlled variables for the SMI and SGO pressures in control 
mode are too great (>  90). 
The controlled variables can be found in the menu under Diagno-
sis/Info → Module -specific→ Regulator measured values → Fidas24.  
• The measured oxygen concentration is much higher than the ex-
pected values.  
This is only a possible indication of a leak. The absence of the states mentioned must not be used to conclude that the analy zer system  is tight.
